        <section class="content article-content mb-6" itemprop="articleBody">
          <p data-start="574" data-end="928">The <a href="https://www.fullstory.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Fullstory</a> connector tools in Optimizely Opal let you interact with your Fullstory account to retrieve user session links, behavioral summaries, and work with Fullstory segments. After you install and configure the Fullstory tools in Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP), the tools become available in <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Opal Chat</a>, <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/39407442255245" target="x_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">agents</a>, and <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/39417564742797" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">workflows</a>.</p><p data-start="930" data-end="985">Complete the following steps to enable Fullstory tools.</p><h2 id="h_01K86CPG4DW356CY1JZDQ3A2DV">Add the Fullstory Opal Tools in OCP<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K86CPG4DW356CY1JZDQ3A2DV"></a></h2><h3 id="h_01KBDFHXKN5JPQX1YWYWE9K49B">Generate a Fullstory API key<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KBDFHXKN5JPQX1YWYWE9K49B"></a></h3><p data-start="1281" data-end="1349">See the <a href="https://help.fullstory.com/hc/en-us/articles/360052021773" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Managing API Keys documentation in the Fullstory help center</a> for steps to generate API keys in Fullstory. Copy the API key as you need it in the following section.</p><div class="note">If you want to use the <a href="#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT">segment export tools,</a> you need an "Admin" level API Key. See the <a href="https://help.fullstory.com/hc/en-us/articles/360052021773#key-permissions" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Key Permissions section in the Fullstory help center</a>.</div><h3 id="h_01KBDFJDGM617D3635BHCPJ2NK">Add the Fullstory Opal Tool in OCP<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KBDFJDGM617D3635BHCPJ2NK"></a></h3><p data-start="1281" data-end="1349">In the OCP <strong>App Directory</strong>, complete the following:</p><ol>
<li data-list-item-id="ec611b421fd7e2e3bc2c9bbe3305d2f8b">
<p>Click on the <strong>Fullstory Opal Tool</strong> connector tool.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1854/1030;" src="/hc/article_attachments/41601100306445" width="1854" height="1030" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed5d26a31ebe7c7a4398993a1102dc0ec">
<p>Click <strong>Install App</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1842/1042;" src="/hc/article_attachments/41601100313613" width="1842" height="1042" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e87f99a5836d78ad5d7a5f03323df7b96">Select the <strong>Settings</strong> tab.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea7e0659bbf1cbe45a31a45bb2d7b756a">Enter your Fullstory API key from the previous <a href="#h_01KBDFHXKN5JPQX1YWYWE9K49B">Generate a Fullstory API key </a>section.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e016f87d9e5ef694524c9f8860bf11eee">
<p>Click <strong data-start="1546" data-end="1554">Save</strong>.</p>
<figure class="wysiwyg-image"><img style="aspect-ratio: 1864/840;" src="/hc/article_attachments/41601100318733" width="1864" height="840" class="img-enlargable"></figure>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7eb9b5abcacab8c3236796a06791fdab">Expand the <strong>AI Features</strong> section.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb460a5868d64c66e3b7b9a8d02c559f0">
<p>(Optional) Toggle <strong data-start="1610" data-end="1648">Enable AI-powered session analysis</strong> if your Fullstory plan includes this capability and you want to use it in Opal.</p>
<div class="note">You may not see all of the <a href="#h_01K848F93CBJAWR0BQN6G7KTRT">Fullstory connector tools</a> available in Opal if you do not have access to AI-powered session analysis.</div>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e43d66e4c12afeafcadd93f556175805e">Click <strong>Save</strong>.<img class="wysiwyg-image img-enlargable" src="/hc/article_attachments/41601100320653" width="1352" height="1014">
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb1139bde7acec22fbae5b6466f718fc4">Expand the <strong>Add to Opal</strong> section and click <strong>Add to Opal</strong> to register the Fullstory tools in the corresponding Opal instance.<img class="wysiwyg-image img-enlargable" src="/hc/article_attachments/41601100325901" width="1330" height="702">
</li>
</ol><h2 id="h_01KBZJPCZTJFQSY0F9E53GM562">Considerations<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KBZJPCZTJFQSY0F9E53GM562"></a></h2><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eb10d8215ba4544ee34ddc9d3fe47f1b2">Ensure that your account is within its tools limit. Go to your Opal account and select <strong data-start="1961" data-end="1970">Tools</strong> to adjust your enabled tools if necessary. See <a href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/39354227438349#h_01KABTB2QXH7YKZNWYCHGB428Q" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Tools page overview</a>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e340cddb7c2e18b871d2d4e88236ce2dc">Fullstory session analysis may take some time, depending on the session length and associated metadata.</li>
</ul><h2 id="h_01K848F93CBJAWR0BQN6G7KTRT">Fullstory connector tools<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01K848F93CBJAWR0BQN6G7KTRT"></a></h2><p>After you add and register the Fullstory connector tools, you can call the following tools in Opal. Click on a tool's name to expand it and learn more about when to use the tool, required and optional parameters, and example prompts on how to call the tool. If you do not provide a required parameter, Opal prompts you for it.</p><h3 id="h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT">Session exports and segment operations<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT"></a></h3><details><summary><code>fullstory_create_segment_export</code> – Creates an export job for a FullStory segment.</summary><p>You can use the <code>fullstory_create_segment_export</code> tool in the following example use cases:</p>
<h4 id="h_01KBR870WY3HZ1G89YJMSW5MGF">Export all user data</h4>
<ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e54e7b13980981b68556e235fdd71a58c">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e21cc94e1061041b678a44590e3157a13">When you need a complete list of all users in your FullStory account.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebb514c1a67ee92c13bc63b7c3db4ded3">To get basic user profile information (like email, display name, first or last seen) for CRM updates or general user analysis.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7291350d3f2af86b38cf561bbee4430b">To understand the overall size and composition of your user base over a specific period.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ecf9e7b48336eb886daae4adb60344199">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="efefb1df743a45b7b087bd2988b6aad0a">
<code>type</code> – <code>TYPE_INDIVIDUAL</code>. To get user information.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecda2431bb4041e93def8be475100efab">
<code>timeRange</code> – A start and end date for the export. For example, <code>{"start": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2024-01-31T23:59:59Z"}</code>)</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efe364a9cd3bad22dc7aceeb8efa11e9f">
<code>format</code> – <code>FORMAT_CSV</code>. For spreadsheet-friendly data.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6f885dccbea2eb25dd99976790b0aa46">
<code>segmentId</code> – <code>"everyone"</code>. To include all users.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ed1ca5071d108d36f6bf9830c5f463470">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="edd48942b6b0344d3fd9dbfd063581253"><em>I need to export all user profiles from FullStory for the last month in CSV format.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed3c7c41485b6542fb24969e5b85fa06d"><em>Can you give me a CSV export of all users, including their email and display name, for the past 90 days?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e46d4014fb46698f04c1eb37b286f0355"><em>Export all individual user data for the current quarter as a CSV file.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="h_01KBR8FWT8XB79P7HNMWM4CMS3">Export specific events for a custom segment </h4>
<ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e0521ca4c50850f2cf0247d0e19dc3a57">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e73cf3f5650946f4b8fb5ef21b520cf43">When you want to analyze specific user actions (events) performed by a particular group of users (segment).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9ba624d256fe27dec30db9ef55c46854">To understand how a defined user segment interacts with a specific feature or completes a critical flow.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3ce5f0d6c8034b29fb19b8a022d402db">For deeper behavioral analysis of a target audience, such as "High-Value Customers" or "Churn Risks."</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e7742161eb42b9b169bbce3c003e0b001">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e534928110ea4a8e06b74e1cb908d02c9">
<code>type</code> – <code>TYPE_EVENT</code>. To export event data.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9be78767c3554555e4965b7af1f72e6c">
<code>timeRange</code> – The start and end date for the export.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e461d484a81c212608a85f4b689d5b159">
<code>format</code> – <code>FORMAT_JSON</code>. For structured data that can be easily parsed by other systems or scripts.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5297952a002a329914f296b2b2241306">
<code>segmentId</code> – The ID of your custom segment. For example, <code>"high-value-customers"</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e75811c77b80abee7eb28a5c0430ba4d0">(Optional) – <code>fields</code> – A comma-separated list of specific event fields you want to include. For example, <code>"event_name,user_id,product_id,event_properties.price"</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ec7e2aea147991e8693b42504d1078143">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1cd4e18886a61e57c7d030b66455456b"><em>Export all 'Product Added to Cart' events for my 'Frequent Shoppers' segment from the last 60 days. I need it in JSON format and please include the product name and price.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e36d63c3353cc5d12775aaca427be8754"><em>Can you get me a JSON export of 'Login Success' events for the 'Admin Users' segment from last week, showing the user ID and login method?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef2a398498a144106b717d193fc50a965"><em>I need a JSON export of 'Form Submission' events for the 'Trial Users' segment from the last 30 days, including the form name and submission status.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="h_01KBR8JX43MX4DE891T8K7F2WP">Export all session data with time zone adjustment</h4>
<ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e54c009d2182ff87ca0aa0a236c42de4b">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e3d8663e618785a4fe0e4b64cd426f76e">When you need detailed session-level information for all users, especially for large datasets that might be processed in a data lake or advanced analytics platform.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9f56bf230550a7c1498d704c688c0b7d">To ensure that all timestamps in your export are aligned with a specific geographic time zone for accurate reporting or analysis across different regions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e15f39bbdc22e0fe12d5305922cb170c7">For comprehensive session replay analysis or to build custom session-level metrics.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="efacf6eeb8de6149a2f0375937b01315e">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eef445558467f2d7ba923675d471b4b66">
<code>type</code> – <code>TYPE_SESSIONS</code>. To export session data.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecdf78ad51b1c92661d991b28fc7cf503">
<code>timeRange</code> – The start and end date for the export.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4216915051eef06bd4cb95c398555095">
<code>format</code> – <code>FORMAT_NDJSON</code>. Newline-delimited JSON, ideal for streaming and processing very large datasets efficiently.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8ab76ab3b9fc052595806cc791eb47e0">
<code>segmentId</code> – <code>"everyone"</code>. To include all sessions from all users.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edf1ff9564fcd6f28012511df579767c1">(Optional) <code>timezone</code> – A valid IANA time zone string. For example, <code>"America/New_York"</code> or  <code>"Europe/London"</code> to adjust timestamps in the export.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e6f732c11ee34e863c36ac98d14af4bdb">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef2bdc495b7b680e5efb3d2550657b4c9"><em>Export all session data for everyone from the last week in NDJSON format, and please adjust the timestamps to 'America/Los_Angeles' time zone.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ea3ca904d5b2a8a18fccab377fedf8f84"><em>I need an NDJSON export of all sessions from the last quarter, adjusted to 'Asia/Tokyo' time zone.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eec7f2d4c5d60f39f23321899ff0f705d"><em>Can you export all user sessions from the past 30 days as NDJSON, with timestamps in 'UTC'?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="h_01KBR8JX4417Q0HFBYQ6H3SBGD">Export page-level events for a specific segment</h4>
<ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eec170da76d85b9e9f90886494efe8bff">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ed9ce66f024c2c51e5d78ef2e1fc19e6f">To understand all events that occurred on specific pages within a segment's sessions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2c4e2398d92a6e6e46f44f5a90869f79">To analyze user journeys and interactions on critical pages (for example, product pages or checkout pages) for a targeted segment.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6d3682c501545f904db1a55b5ba7727e">For optimizing page performance or identifying friction points on key conversion paths.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9d4c71389b8830e7b9f0374116ea8e48">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="edd19460bc96ffc60027e382075147474">
<code>type</code> – <code>TYPE_PAGES</code>. To export page-level event data.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec82baeb41feb09694d8048fc91e84c2f">
<code>timeRange</code> – The start and end date for the export.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb581b747bae19890803d8dbcb0d06d5f">
<code>format</code> – <code>FORMAT_CSV</code>. For easy review of page URLs and associated events.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5e81ed08dab6657843f6b19eac2ceb80">
<code>segmentId</code> – The ID of your custom segment. For example, <code>"blog-readers"</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e083e1c046d27bd707268ecda7e1fb087">(Optional) <code>fields</code> – A comma-separated list of specific page-related fields you want to include. For example, <code>"url,referrer,page_title"</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="effd004d34229fdcda5a283e439dab9b6">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efbc3087e3b12b02f1553cc15db29d69b"><em>I want to get all page-related events for users in my 'Blog Readers' segment from the last 30 days. Please provide this as a CSV file, including the page URL and referrer.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed6155fea09681cf59d10db446e93f77e"><em>Export page event data for the 'Checkout Abandoners' segment from last month in CSV, showing the page URL and any error messages.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e46ff170332b4d6eacfa80197709e488f"><em>Can you give me a CSV export of page events for the 'Product Page Viewers' segment from the last 7 days, including the page title and URL?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>fullstory_get_operation_status</code> – Gets the status of a FullStory export operation. <strong>When to use</strong><ul>

<li data-list-item-id="e05aa4187a75e044346d0eb3316632644">To periodically check if a long-running export job has finished processing.</li>

<li data-list-item-id="e53f9824b37ff1e531021aeb0c32443b8">To verify if an export operation encountered any issues or failed.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea940933cc2ecbac28bbd09792287ab14">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="eec34b84e57b27067e153ddb3233ac230">

<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e080573fa66a7e7bea5017c3f522ee5b4">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e19d1f25881c8640fc1d6f7ef6d4206ae">
<em>What is the status of my FullStory export with operation ID </em><code><em>U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRVZCdxdSeV</em></code><em>?</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee2023f7dc434f697a5e180ad896ebc62">
<em>Is the export job </em><code><em>U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRVZCdxdSeV</em></code><em> complete yet?</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec7f311c9393d381e674cc58e02b452f6">
<em>Check the progress of operation </em><code><em>U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRVZCdxdSeV</em></code><em> and tell me if it is ready to download.</em>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>fullstory_get_search_export_results</code> – Gets a temporary download URL for a completed FullStory search export. <li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea8c213dbc6beddd50ccab61b5604e593">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e10d958efaef9f42722d8cdc9fd736c08">After a search export operation. For example, from a FullStory search API call, (not <code>create_segment_export</code>) has completed and you have received its unique <code>id</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e48a7dc69cefc6fbcdf662c863702ce11">When you need to access the actual exported data file from a FullStory search.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5ae87b9a9db6e34d398453520ee020d0">To obtain the temporary URL to download the results of a previously initiated search export.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e21595fc2ee1c5020b685e7a01a631a42">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="eaab1d850fdd43e01e8b007a5c5759bc6">
<code>id</code> – The unique identifier of the search export. This ID is typically returned as a result of a <code>SEARCH_EXPORT</code> operation within FullStory.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e43e3ae02c8e2c21e5c84323c487dc12c">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ea58febb425700b2ce8396c9cd5a1e3dc">
<em>Can I get the download link for search export ID </em><code><em>U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3</em></code><em>?</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ecd56d0dc3bd5cdd9834ed1e66d5e7786">
<em>Please provide the results for my search export with ID </em><code><em>U0VBUkmIX1VYU</em></code><em>.</em>

<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e00343f00c23bf4b9dfd5cbcd123a2c20">
<em>I have a completed search export with ID </em><code><em>U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRV</em></code><em>. Give me the download URL.</em>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>fullstory_get_segment</code> – Returns detailed information for a specific FullStory segment. This includes metadata like the segment's name, who created it, when it was created, and a direct URL to view it in the FullStory UI.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e4fba85fa30f301244d116d803d21a2b0">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ec8300f3ab9225b36bb25ffe53832f145">When you have a segment ID (a custom one or a built-in one like "everyone"), and you need to retrieve more information about that specific segment.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6e89ebbd81e21f0ae00658598c275f09">To verify the existence of a segment before using it in other operations. For instance, before exporting data from it.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2bca13b407bf8260bdced2e2c4912640">To understand the properties and metadata of a segment, such as its creation date or the user who created it.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7147f5d7f8293a5195f62ce79be155a2">When a user asks for details about a segment by its name or ID.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e84593c7af7d6127621c07ff28bc6e9a9">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e1742cd3399e717534e87394c7eca3977">
<code>id</code> – The unique identifier of the segment you want to retrieve details for. This can be a custom segment ID (for example, <code>"12345abcdefg"</code>) or a built-in segment ID like <code>"everyone"</code>.</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e40db18288637bc6172e5b264fc6c3630">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8d3979fda30e4e6c89e86fbcb32110d9"><em>Tell me about the 'everyone' segment.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed26f2018b7c693e0437bf8abb48ffcec">
<em>What are the details for segment ID </em><code><em>12345abcdefg</em></code><em>?</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed028f4a0e3ef4778b032519cf7dd4e88"><em>Can you provide information on the segment named 'High-Value Customers'?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed40e5c5a73cc0824358c20b79e3bf32f">
<em>Show me the creation date and creator of segment </em><code><em>my-new-segment-id</em></code><em>.</em>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>fullstory_list_segments</code> – Lists all segments available to your FullStory API key.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e49afa226574d59bb299c90e60862104c">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e316651b850f8e1f18f335ad8f8d456f3">When you need to discover all segments that exist in your FullStory account.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb9262690e66320ad1019ef93aba6a838">To find the <code>id</code> of a segment that you want to use in other tools. For instance, the <code>fullstory_create_segment_export</code> tool or the <code>fullstory_get_segment</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e45753b72ba0f70e6cc211a857353bd91">To get an overview of your organization's segmentation structure.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e900ee234682e9ddc265a57fdfdb38545">If you want to browse segments created by a specific team member.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e417109cbe6d45523cc4ce7ea3f4df32a">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e8cd2501f69d6481ece07274c70e9d35c">(Optional) <code>limit</code> – The maximum number of segments to return, between 1 and 100, defaults to 20. Useful for controlling the size of the response.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e73c0000658abbe23d86fcb472161bd87">(Optional) <code>paginationToken</code> – A token obtained from a previous <code>fullstory_list_segments</code> call to retrieve the next page of results.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1fc9c059a92acb59cc40d5c33370c9c5">(Optional) <code>creator</code> – An email address to filter segments by the user who created them.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e914e0a6e11dd526bc044023f6d695986">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9c1b4840551264008bd1f6cb19e6d9b9"><em>List all FullStory segments.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e731cb320c7451b7f206d9c8352ac3de8">
<em>Show me the segments created by </em><code><em>optimizer@optimizely.com</em></code><em>.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee2f18b4169d87be13508c57d32d614c3"><em>What are the top 10 segments in FullStory?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e58494fdf3ee7ebde87783644bc0400e1"><em>Can you list all segments and paginate the results?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb56440f8170df1e94f842486dda49844"><em>I need to see all segments, but only 50 at a time.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><h3 id="h_01KB06HH4A791AQQXN762KWMD0">Session summaries and behavioral analysis<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KB06HH4A791AQQXN762KWMD0"></a></h3><details><summary><code>fullstory_get_session_quick_summary</code> – Gets a quick AI-generated summary of a FullStory session recording. This tool provides brief, focused insights into user behavior and session outcomes, covering what the user did, whether they achieved their goal, and any issues encountered.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e79ef9ebe9148cadcc7a452cab1083b1f">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>

<template id="tmpl-partial-article-list-sections">
  <% if (sections.length) { %>
    <ul class="list-none pl-3 mb-0 font-size-base collapse" id="<%= id %>" :class="{ 'is-visible': isOpen }" data-parent="<%= parentId %>">
      <% sections.forEach(function(section) { %>
        <li class="font-medium" x-data="toggle({ isOpen: <%= !!section.isActive %> })" @collapse:show.stop="open" @collapse:hide.stop="close">

          
          <div class="flex justify-content-between align-items-center">
            <a class="flex-1 py-2 text-inherit font-semibold" :class="{ 'text-inherit': !isOpen }" href="<%= section.html_url %>">
              <%= section.name %>
            </a>
            <button class="p-2 ml-1 not-a-button border-radius transition cursor-pointer hover:bg-gray-200" :class="{ 'is-active': isOpen }" :aria-expanded="isOpen" data-toggle="collapse" data-target="#section-<%= section.id %>">
              <svg class="text-inherit fill-current pointer-events-none" :class="{ 'rotate-180': isOpen }" width="12px" height="12px" viewBox="0 0 324 190" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-hidden="true">
                <path d="M162,190 C156,190 150,187 146,183 L7,38 C-2,29 -2,15 7,7 C16,-2 30,-2 39,7 L162,135 L285,7 C293,-2 308,-2 317,7 C326,15 326,29 317,38 L178,183 C174,187 168,190 162,190 Z"></path>
              </svg>
            </button>
          </div>

          
          <%= partial('partial-article-list-sections', {
            id: 'section-' + section.id,
            parentId: '#' + id,
            sections: section.sections,
            activeCategoryId: activeCategoryId,
            activeSectionId: activeSectionId,
            activeArticleId: activeArticleId,
            partial: partial
          }) %>

          
          <% if (section.articles.length) { %>
            <ul class="list-none font-size-md pl-0 mb-0 collapse" :class="{ 'is-visible': isOpen }" id="section-<%= section.id %>" data-parent="#<%= id %>">
              <% section.articles.forEach(function(article) { %>
                <li>
                  <a class="block px-3 py-2 text-inherit border-radius transition<% if (article.isActive) { %> bg-gray-100<% } %>" href="<%= article.html_url %>">
                    <%= article.title %>
                  </a>
                </li>
              <% }); %>
            </ul>
          <% } %>

        </li>
      <% }); %>
    </ul>
  <% } %>
</template>


<template id="tmpl-partial-section-list-sections">
  <% if (sections.length) { %>
    <ul class="list-unstyled font-size-md<% if (parent.hasOwnProperty('parent_section_id')) { %> pl-4 mb-0<% } %>">
      <% sections.slice(0, maxSections).forEach(function(section) { %>
        <li>
          <a class="block py-2 text-inherit<% if (section.isActive) { %> border-left border-left-primary border-left-4 -ml-4 pl-3<% } %>" href="<%= section.html_url %>">
            <%= section.name %>
          </a>
          <%= partial('partial-section-list-sections', { parent: section, sections: section.sections, maxSections: maxSections, partial: partial }) %>
        </li>
      <% }); %>
      <% if (sections.length > maxSections) { %>
        <li>
          <a class="block py-2 text-inherit" href="<%= parent.html_url %>">
            See more
          </a>
        </li>
      <% } %>
    </ul>
  <% } %>
</template>

The [Fullstory](https://www.fullstory.com) connector tools in Optimizely Opal let you interact with your Fullstory account to retrieve user session links, behavioral summaries, and work with Fullstory segments. After you install and configure the Fullstory tools in Optimizely Connect Platform (OCP), the tools become available in [Opal Chat](/hc/en-us/articles/36343492268813), [agents](/hc/en-us/articles/39407442255245), and [workflows](/hc/en-us/articles/39417564742797).

Complete the following steps to enable Fullstory tools.

## Add the Fullstory Opal Tools in OCP[](#h_01K86CPG4DW356CY1JZDQ3A2DV)

### Generate a Fullstory API key[](#h_01KBDFHXKN5JPQX1YWYWE9K49B)

See the [Managing API Keys documentation in the Fullstory help center](https://help.fullstory.com/hc/en-us/articles/360052021773) for steps to generate API keys in Fullstory. Copy the API key as you need it in the following section.

If you want to use the [segment export tools,](#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT) you need an "Admin" level API Key. See the [Key Permissions section in the Fullstory help center](https://help.fullstory.com/hc/en-us/articles/360052021773#key-permissions).

### Add the Fullstory Opal Tool in OCP[](#h_01KBDFJDGM617D3635BHCPJ2NK)

In the OCP **App Directory**, complete the following:

1.  Click on the **Fullstory Opal Tool** connector tool.
    
    ![](/hc/article_attachments/41601100306445)
    
2.  Click **Install App**.
    
    ![](/hc/article_attachments/41601100313613)
    
3.  Select the **Settings** tab.
4.  Enter your Fullstory API key from the previous [Generate a Fullstory API key](#h_01KBDFHXKN5JPQX1YWYWE9K49B) section.
5.  Click **Save**.
    
    ![](/hc/article_attachments/41601100318733)
    
6.  Expand the **AI Features** section.
7.  (Optional) Toggle **Enable AI-powered session analysis** if your Fullstory plan includes this capability and you want to use it in Opal.
    
    You may not see all of the [Fullstory connector tools](#h_01K848F93CBJAWR0BQN6G7KTRT) available in Opal if you do not have access to AI-powered session analysis.
    
8.  Click **Save**.![](/hc/article_attachments/41601100320653)
9.  Expand the **Add to Opal** section and click **Add to Opal** to register the Fullstory tools in the corresponding Opal instance.![](/hc/article_attachments/41601100325901)

## Fullstory connector tools[](#h_01K848F93CBJAWR0BQN6G7KTRT)

After you add and register the Fullstory connector tools, you can call the following tools in Opal. Click on a tool's name to expand it and learn more about when to use the tool, required and optional parameters, and example prompts on how to call the tool. If you do not provide a required parameter, Opal prompts you for it.

### Session exports and segment operations[](#h_01KB06H8D76MKT758BQ5AFWZNT)

`fullstory_create_segment_export` – Creates an export job for a FullStory segment.

You can use the `fullstory_create_segment_export` tool in the following example use cases:

#### Export all user data

*   **When to use**
    *   When you need a complete list of all users in your FullStory account.
    *   To get basic user profile information (like email, display name, first or last seen) for CRM updates or general user analysis.
    *   To understand the overall size and composition of your user base over a specific period.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `type` – `TYPE_INDIVIDUAL`. To get user information.
    *   `timeRange` – A start and end date for the export. For example, `{"start": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2024-01-31T23:59:59Z"}`)
    *   `format` – `FORMAT_CSV`. For spreadsheet-friendly data.
    *   `segmentId` – `"everyone"`. To include all users.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _I need to export all user profiles from FullStory for the last month in CSV format._
    *   _Can you give me a CSV export of all users, including their email and display name, for the past 90 days?_
    *   _Export all individual user data for the current quarter as a CSV file._

#### Export specific events for a custom segment 

*   **When to use**
    *   When you want to analyze specific user actions (events) performed by a particular group of users (segment).
    *   To understand how a defined user segment interacts with a specific feature or completes a critical flow.
    *   For deeper behavioral analysis of a target audience, such as "High-Value Customers" or "Churn Risks."
*   **Parameters**
    *   `type` – `TYPE_EVENT`. To export event data.
    *   `timeRange` – The start and end date for the export.
    *   `format` – `FORMAT_JSON`. For structured data that can be easily parsed by other systems or scripts.
    *   `segmentId` – The ID of your custom segment. For example, `"high-value-customers"`.
    *   (Optional) – `fields` – A comma-separated list of specific event fields you want to include. For example, `"event_name,user_id,product_id,event_properties.price"`.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Export all 'Product Added to Cart' events for my 'Frequent Shoppers' segment from the last 60 days. I need it in JSON format and please include the product name and price._
    *   _Can you get me a JSON export of 'Login Success' events for the 'Admin Users' segment from last week, showing the user ID and login method?_
    *   _I need a JSON export of 'Form Submission' events for the 'Trial Users' segment from the last 30 days, including the form name and submission status._

#### Export all session data with time zone adjustment

*   **When to use**
    *   When you need detailed session-level information for all users, especially for large datasets that might be processed in a data lake or advanced analytics platform.
    *   To ensure that all timestamps in your export are aligned with a specific geographic time zone for accurate reporting or analysis across different regions.
    *   For comprehensive session replay analysis or to build custom session-level metrics.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `type` – `TYPE_SESSIONS`. To export session data.
    *   `timeRange` – The start and end date for the export.
    *   `format` – `FORMAT_NDJSON`. Newline-delimited JSON, ideal for streaming and processing very large datasets efficiently.
    *   `segmentId` – `"everyone"`. To include all sessions from all users.
    *   (Optional) `timezone` – A valid IANA time zone string. For example, `"America/New_York"` or  `"Europe/London"` to adjust timestamps in the export.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Export all session data for everyone from the last week in NDJSON format, and please adjust the timestamps to 'America/Los\_Angeles' time zone._
    *   _I need an NDJSON export of all sessions from the last quarter, adjusted to 'Asia/Tokyo' time zone._
    *   _Can you export all user sessions from the past 30 days as NDJSON, with timestamps in 'UTC'?_

#### Export page-level events for a specific segment

*   **When to use**
    *   To understand all events that occurred on specific pages within a segment's sessions.
    *   To analyze user journeys and interactions on critical pages (for example, product pages or checkout pages) for a targeted segment.
    *   For optimizing page performance or identifying friction points on key conversion paths.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `type` – `TYPE_PAGES`. To export page-level event data.
    *   `timeRange` – The start and end date for the export.
    *   `format` – `FORMAT_CSV`. For easy review of page URLs and associated events.
    *   `segmentId` – The ID of your custom segment. For example, `"blog-readers"`.
    *   (Optional) `fields` – A comma-separated list of specific page-related fields you want to include. For example, `"url,referrer,page_title"`.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _I want to get all page-related events for users in my 'Blog Readers' segment from the last 30 days. Please provide this as a CSV file, including the page URL and referrer._
    *   _Export page event data for the 'Checkout Abandoners' segment from last month in CSV, showing the page URL and any error messages._
    *   _Can you give me a CSV export of page events for the 'Product Page Viewers' segment from the last 7 days, including the page title and URL?_

`fullstory_get_operation_status` – Gets the status of a FullStory export operation. Use this to check the progress of segment exports created with the `create_segment_export` tool. When the export is complete, the response includes a download URL for the exported data.

*   **When to use**
    *   Immediately after you have initiated a segment export using the `fullstory_create_segment_export` tool and received an `operationId`.
    *   To periodically check if a long-running export job has finished processing.
    *   When you need to retrieve the temporary download URL for a completed export.
    *   To verify if an export operation encountered any issues or failed.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `operationId` – The unique identifier for the export operation that was returned when you created the export.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _What is the status of my FullStory export with operation ID_ `_U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRVZCdxdSeV_`_?_
    *   _Is the export job_ `_U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRVZCdxdSeV_` _complete yet?_
    *   _Check the progress of operation_ `_U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRVZCdxdSeV_` _and tell me if it is ready to download._

`fullstory_get_search_export_results` – Gets a temporary download URL for a completed FullStory search export. This endpoint provides a download link for completed search exports, which are typically initiated by other FullStory search-related operations.

*   **When to use**
    *   After a search export operation. For example, from a FullStory search API call, (not `create_segment_export`) has completed and you have received its unique `id`.
    *   When you need to access the actual exported data file from a FullStory search.
    *   To obtain the temporary URL to download the results of a previously initiated search export.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `id` – The unique identifier of the search export. This ID is typically returned as a result of a `SEARCH_EXPORT` operation within FullStory.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Can I get the download link for search export ID_ `_U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3_`_?_
    *   _Please provide the results for my search export with ID_ `_U0VBUkmIX1VYU_`_._
    *   _I have a completed search export with ID_ `_U0VBUkmIX1VYUE9SVFplcmRteUlPV3YyV3RnRV_`_. Give me the download URL._

`fullstory_get_segment` – Returns detailed information for a specific FullStory segment. This includes metadata like the segment's name, who created it, when it was created, and a direct URL to view it in the FullStory UI.

*   **When to use**
    *   When you have a segment ID (a custom one or a built-in one like "everyone"), and you need to retrieve more information about that specific segment.
    *   To verify the existence of a segment before using it in other operations. For instance, before exporting data from it.
    *   To understand the properties and metadata of a segment, such as its creation date or the user who created it.
    *   When a user asks for details about a segment by its name or ID.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `id` – The unique identifier of the segment you want to retrieve details for. This can be a custom segment ID (for example, `"12345abcdefg"`) or a built-in segment ID like `"everyone"`.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Tell me about the 'everyone' segment._
    *   _What are the details for segment ID_ `_12345abcdefg_`_?_
    *   _Can you provide information on the segment named 'High-Value Customers'?_
    *   _Show me the creation date and creator of segment_ `_my-new-segment-id_`_._

`fullstory_list_segments` – Lists all segments available to your FullStory API key.

*   **When to use**
    *   When you need to discover all segments that exist in your FullStory account.
    *   To find the `id` of a segment that you want to use in other tools. For instance, the `fullstory_create_segment_export` tool or the `fullstory_get_segment` tool.
    *   To get an overview of your organization's segmentation structure.
    *   If you want to browse segments created by a specific team member.
*   **Parameters**
    *   (Optional) `limit` – The maximum number of segments to return, between 1 and 100, defaults to 20. Useful for controlling the size of the response.
    *   (Optional) `paginationToken` – A token obtained from a previous `fullstory_list_segments` call to retrieve the next page of results.
    *   (Optional) `creator` – An email address to filter segments by the user who created them.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List all FullStory segments._
    *   _Show me the segments created by_ `_optimizer@optimizely.com_`_._
    *   _What are the top 10 segments in FullStory?_
    *   _Can you list all segments and paginate the results?_
    *   _I need to see all segments, but only 50 at a time._

### Session summaries and behavioral analysis[](#h_01KB06HH4A791AQQXN762KWMD0)

`fullstory_get_session_quick_summary` – Gets a quick AI-generated summary of a FullStory session recording. This tool provides brief, focused insights into user behavior and session outcomes, covering what the user did, whether they achieved their goal, and any issues encountered.

*   **When to use**
    *   For rapid triage or initial assessment of a user session to quickly understand its main points.
    *   During daily reviews of multiple sessions to get a concise overview.
    *   When you need a brief summary (two to three sentences) for reporting or sharing with stakeholders.
    *   To quickly identify if a session was successful, problematic, or inconclusive.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `sessionId` – The unique identifier for the session to analyze. This ID consists of two parts, `userId` and `sessionNumber`, separated by a colon. For instance, `"1234567890:0987654321"`. 
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Give me a quick summary of FullStory session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_._
    *   _Summarize what happened in session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_._
    *   _What is a brief overview of session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_?_
    *   _Can you provide a quick AI summary for session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_?_

`fullstory_get_session_behavior_summary` – Gets a detailed behavioral pattern analysis of a FullStory session recording.     *   To identify potential user personas (for example, "power user," "first-timer," or "explorer") within a session.
    *   For UX researchers and product teams looking to analyze feature usage, navigation styles, and engagement levels.
    *   To understand the likely goals and motivations behind a user's actions in a session.
    *   When investigating specific user journeys for optimization opportunities.
*   **Parameters**
    *   `sessionId` – The unique identifier for the session to analyze. This ID consists of two parts, `userId` and `sessionNumber`, separated by a colon. For instance, `"1234567890:0987654321"`. 
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Analyze the user behavior in FullStory session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_._
    *   _Give me a detailed behavioral summary of session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_._
    *   _What kind of user behavior patterns can you identify in FullStory session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_?_
    *   _Provide a behavioral analysis for session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_._
    *   _I need to understand the user's intent and engagement in session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_. Can you provide a behavioral summary?_

`fullstory_get_session_support_summary` – Gets a detailed, support-focused summary of a FullStory session recording.     *   When you need to understand complex customer issues in detail, including user intentions, frustrations, and the final outcome of the session.

    *   _Provide a detailed support analysis of session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_`_._
    *   _I need to understand the problems encountered in session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_` _for a support ticket._
    *   _Can you summarize session_ `_1234567890:0987654321_` _with a focus on support recommendations for our support team can take?_

My post-prompt is 'List all pages visited, the entry and exit points, and any observed navigation patterns (for example, linear, exploratory, search-driven).'_

### User sessions and replay links[](#h_01KB06HP2SXSCR7EE1AW2PD088)

`fullstory_list_sessions` – Lists session replay URLs for a user in FullStory.

*   **When to use**
    *   When you need to find session replays for a specific user to troubleshoot an issue they reported.
    *   To get a list of recent user activity for customer support or behavioral analysis.
    *   When a user asks to see all or a certain number of sessions for a particular user, identified by their email or user ID.
    *   To access session replays directly to investigate user journeys or pain points.
*   **Parameters**
    
    You must provide an `uid` or `email`. If both are provided, the tool returns a union of results for both parameters.
    
    *   `uid` – The user's ID as set through `FS.identify` in your application. For example, `"user123"`.
    *   `email` – The user's email address as set through `FS.identify` or `FS.setUserVars`. For example, `"user@example.com"`.
    *   (Optional) `limit` – Maximum number of sessions to return. Must be between 1 and 100, defaults to 20 if not specified.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _List the last 10 sessions for user_ `_john.doe@example.com_`_._
    *   _Show me the sessions for user ID_ `_12345_`_._
    *   _Can you find recent sessions for_ `_jane.smith@example.com_`_?_
    *   _I need to see the last 5 sessions for user_ `_user_abc_`_._
    *   _What are all the sessions for_ `_optimizer@optimizely.com_`_?_

`fullstory_visit_profile` – Analyzes user session data to provide UX insights and support intelligence. This advanced analysis tool combines FullStory session replay data with AI-powered analysis to identify user behavior patterns, pain points, and technical issues across multiple sessions.

*   **When to use**
    *   When you need a holistic view of a user's experience across several sessions, rather than just a single session.
    *   For customer support teams preparing for a call or investigating a user's history of issues and interactions.
    *   For UX researchers to identify recurring behavior patterns, common frustrations, and overall user journey trends for a specific user.
    *   To proactively identify struggling users or those with persistent technical problems.
    *   When you need a summary that integrates insights from multiple sessions, including user goals, frustration indicators, technical errors, and actionable recommendations.
*   **Parameters**
    
    You must provide either an `uid` or `email`. You cannot provide both.
    
    *   `uid` – Your application's user ID for the user to analyze. For example, `"user123"`.
    *   `email` – The email address of the user to analyze. For example, `"user@example.com"`.
    *   (Optional) `limit` – Maximum number of recent sessions to analyze. Must be between 1 and 20, defaults to 5. Analyzing more sessions provides richer insights but takes longer.
    *   (Optional) `llm` – An object to configure the AI analysis with the following custom prompts:
        *   `pre_prompt` (string) – Context prompt to guide the analysis perspective. For example, `"You are a customer success specialist analyzing user behavior."`.
        *   `post_prompt` (string): Output format and focus guidance. For example, `"Focus on identifying opportunities for user engagement and success."`.
        *   `temperature` (number) – Analysis creativity level (0.0-1.0, default 0.2). Lower values for factual analysis, higher for creative insights.
*   **Example prompts**
    *   _Analyze the FullStory profile for_ `_john.doe@example.com_`_._
    *   _Give me a comprehensive UX insight report for user ID_ `_user123_` _based on their last 10 sessions._
